summary: Independently verify the classification readout and ADR 0017 table, then merge both workflows into one ranked list and refute it

rA.selection_rule:
Source of metadata: mlruns/1..9 is an artifact-only store. `find` finds no meta.yaml and no tags/ directory under any of the 3,207 run dirs, so the tags the task names can't be read from disk. I took them from the read-only SQLite snapshot sync/mlflow.db.windows-2026-09-29.bak, opened with file:...?mode=ro&immutable=1. It holds 3,730 runs, the newest from 2026-09-29. Experiments 1..9 are TRIDENT/<base dataset>. The mirrors are experiments 10 and 11 (TRIDENT/mirror/imputation and TRIDENT/mirror/classification), and neither has a folder under mlruns, so no mirror can enter an artifact-based count. I did not touch incoming.db.

Steps:
(1) Artifact filter: no artifacts/imputation and no per_column_imputation.csv, and the run has artifacts/metrics/raw_fold_metrics.csv. That leaves 81 classification-shaped dirs, plus 9 single_split dirs that have no fold file.
(2) Join to the snapshot. Keep task=classification, run_role=parent, is_mirror=false, no mlflow.parentRunId, status FINISHED, lifecycle active, is_optuna=false.
(3) Defaults: provenance.json split_strategy=cross_validation, cv_folds=3, seed=42; hyperparameters.json EPOCHS_PRE=300, EPOCH_FINE=150, with no LR_SCHEDULER key (tag lr_scheduler=cosine_legacy, backfilled).

Result: 55 runs covering all 45 variants (9 tables x 0/20/40/60/80nan). Duplicates exist only at 00nan: two per dataset (2026-08-04 at commit dee4d6f, and 2026-09-08/09 at c0a909b), three for vehicle (adds e31238b8 at 59d18eb). Dedup rule: keep the latest start_time per variant, giving 45 runs.

Commits of the kept runs: all 00nan at c0a909b, all 20-80nan at 6d49ed5. `git diff --stat c0a909bd 6d49ed5f -- src main.py train.py opt.py` is empty (6d49ed5 is a docs-only commit), so every kept run used the same training code.

Score per run = mean of the 3 per-fold f1_macro values in raw_fold_metrics.csv. For all 55 runs it equals the snapshot's cv/test/f1_macro/mean, so these are test-fold scores, not validation scores.

Excluded:
- 5 dirs absent from the snapshot: 2-fold, 3-epoch smoke tests.
- 8 LR_SCHEDULER sweep runs (seed 42, 200/150, vehicle and credit-g 00nan).
- 12 seed-420 sweep runs.
- 1 vehicle run at 40/40 epochs.
- 9 single_split 40/40 runs.
- 5 runs that are in the snapshot only, with no artifacts: 40/40 epochs or FAILED (2f53aa9e, 62dd265c, 38f9de57, d35ee649, 128e59c3).

The newest classification run anywhere is 2026-09-10 00:31 (GMT-3), so the 09-29 snapshot covers them all. Any classification runs that exist only on the server side can't be seen without incoming.db.

comparability_caveats: Data split: the fork uses 3-fold StratifiedKFold (seed 42) and carves validation out of each fold's 2/3 train+val (validation_ratio = 0.1/(1-1/3) = 0.15, src/training/data.py:226-227; the same code is at 6d49ed5f data.py:102-103). That is about 56.7% train, 10% validation and 33.3% test per fold, and the score is the 3-fold mean. The paper uses one stratified 80/10/10 split with seed 42 and scores a 10% test set.

Tuning: the fork runs are untuned built-in defaults (DIM 128, HIDDEN_DIM 16, HEADS 16, LAYERS 2, DIM_FEED 32, DROPOUT 0.2, BATCH 256, LR_PRE 3.4e-4, WD_PRE 5e-3, PROB_MASCARA 0.5, LR_FINE 1e-3, WD_FINE 1.9e-3, 300/150 epochs; src/training/types.py:201-202), identical for every dataset. Paper TRIDENT was tuned on test macro-F1 (owner, 2026-10-15; Wiki references/trident-paper.md:206), while the baselines were tuned on validation through TabZilla (20 Optuna trials). The paper's margins are optimistic, and the fork's per-dataset values aren't comparable to tuned ones.

Hyperparameter files: none were read. Every run's logged hyperparameters.json equals the code defaults. `git log -- datasets/hiperparams` shows the first file landed on 2026-09-11, and it is an imputation config. No classification <dataset>.json exists now either. Commit c0a909b restored the 300/150 defaults explicitly to match the 2026-08-04 batch run, which also used the built-in defaults.

LR schedule: every kept run is lr_scheduler=cosine_legacy (a backfilled tag; hyperparameters.json has no LR_SCHEDULER key, so these runs predate ADR 0003). cosine_legacy is CosineAnnealingLR(T_max=epochs) stepped per batch, a sawtooth. ADR 0003:33 calls it 'the published behaviour', so it matches the authors' code rather than diverging from it.

C1 leak: StandardScaler and LabelEncoder are fit on the whole frame before any fold exists (6d49ed5f src/training/data.py:43,53-54; current data.py:61,70-73; docs/BACKLOG.md:147-156). Test-fold statistics reach training. The upstream code does the same, but it inflates results relative to a per-fold pipeline.
Checkpoint: fine-tuning restores the state with the best validation loss (6d49ed5f src/training/finetuning.py:168-175). The paper does not state its checkpoint rule.

The fork's 0% mean (0.8577) beats LightGBM (0.8494), the paper's TRIDENT (0.8426) and its no-pretraining variant (0.8533). 0% is where the C1 scaler leak and the 3-fold-mean estimator against a single 10% test set matter most, so this is not a credible win.
LABELS=4 is logged for every run, including 26-class letter and 10-class pendigits. BACKLOG C3 (docs/BACKLOG.md:22,172) says the parameter is logged but never used, so it doesn't bear on the results.

Provenance: the LR-sweep runs carry the same git commit tag (6d49ed5) yet log LR_SCHEDULER, so the commit tag records HEAD, not the working tree. The default runs' hyperparameters.json lacking LR_SCHEDULER is the evidence they ran the committed pre-ADR-0003 code.

Run timing: 0% comes from runs started 2026-09-08 23:25 to 2026-09-09 01:00 GMT-3, and 20-80% from runs started 2026-09-09 06:48 to 17:01 GMT-3. The code is identical (empty src diff between c0a909b and 6d49ed5).

Fold reuse: the NaN levels share the same StratifiedKFold folds (same rows and labels, seed 42), so levels are paired within the fork. The paper's per-level variants also share one split, but each missingness level is drawn independently.

Store coverage: run metadata came from the 2026-09-29 snapshot, not the live store. Any classification runs made later on gorgona8 are invisible without sync/incoming.db, which was off-limits. All 90 classification artifact dirs on disk are accounted for.

rC.config_and_seeds:
ADR 0017's Outcome table (0017:139-165) uses E35: seeds 42, 7 and 13, five folds. Each cell is the mean over the three seeds of the CV means, lower is better. The model's score is ADR 0015's K readout (the checkpoint chosen on the validation gaps). E35 cells ran with --decode_checkpoint loss --score_induced_checkpoint, so K is the `induced_checkpoint` column. E36 states K "equal to a default run to the last digit" (EXPERIMENTATION_LOG:1089-1090). The five promoted files were in force: E35 credit-g_40nan seed 42 shows PROB_MASCARA 0.2 and LR_DECODE 0.0087 in hyperparameters.json. The bar is the best of mean_mode, knn5, knn10, hgb and lgbm, picked per variant by the 3-seed mean (0017:27-32). missForest is outside the bar.

Two caveats on calling that table "today's default":
- ADR 0018 (2026-10-07 09:15) landed after the table. pendigits_20nan and letter_20nan now default to the bigger encoder (4 layers, feed-forward 256, LayerNorm), so E35 reads the old encoder on those two.
- E39 may change the five promoted files.

The docs contain no paired verdicts against the ADR 0017 bar or missForest. Those live only in the store (gap_to_best_baseline*, gap_to_missforest*), and I could not read it: sync/incoming.db is off-limits and the other .db files date from Sep 29. I rebuilt the verdicts from the mlruns artifacts (raw_fold_metrics.csv, read as plain files, stdlib Python, no project imports).

- (A) E35: all 63 parents found, one per variant and seed. They reproduce every model and bar cell of ADR 0017 to 3 dp (42 of 42).
  - lgbm is not in these artifacts, because the backfills wrote only to the store (0016:154, 0017:87). Where lgbm sets the bar (6 induced, 8 masked) I paired against hgb instead. lgbm is at or below hgb, so a 'better' verdict against this proxy is an upper bound for the model; 'no difference' and 'worse' are safe.
  - missForest per-fold values do not exist for seeds 42/7/13, so there are no paired missForest verdicts on E35. ADR 0017's 0.016 inductive-versus-transductive band is the only tie criterion there.
- (B) Seeds 101/202/303, today's default: E34's K readout (63 cells, 2026-10-03) for 19 variants, and E38's ALL arm for pendigits_20nan and letter_20nan.
  - ADR 0018 verification (0018:50) says default runs equal E38 ALL to the last digit, and I reproduce E38's 0.3331→0.3203 and 0.4590→0.4331.
  - The four ADR 0007 baselines come from E34 and are identical to E38's on every fold (max difference 0.0). lgbm and missForest come from E38's artifacts.

rD.setup:
The 'ice' field holds ice_seq, not the template's own transform. ice_seq uses the template MiceImputer's fit: MissForestImputer rounds with BayesianRidge for numerical columns and LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000) for categorical ones. That fit matches sklearn IterativeImputer(BayesianRidge) to the last digit. The test rows are then filled the way sklearn's transform does it: the model of round 1, then round 2, and so on up to the kept round, with no stop rule. One difference from sklearn: the number of rounds is the template's still_converging count (3 to 10 per fold), not sklearn's fixed max_iter=10. Matching sklearn on that count gives agreement within 1.4e-9 on biodeg_20nan and kc2_20nan (10 rounds) and within 1e-12 on vehicle_20nan against sklearn(max_iter=6). Running default sklearn on vehicle_20nan differs by up to 1.19, so reproducing these numbers needs the round count set. The template's own fill (MissForestImputer.impute replays the kept round's models on test rows that start at the means) is reported in every row's note as template_replay. It scores 2.0 to 18.8 on the numerical tables (see caveats).

Pre-registered versus post-hoc. The condexp and SoftImpute rules and the 0.003 tie band are frozen in impprobe_arms_v1_preregistered.py (mtime 11:02:27). That predates the first score, impprobe_knncheck.jsonl at 11:02:58.
- condexp: pairwise-complete covariance around the training observed means, turned into a correlation, shrunk as R <- 0.9R + 0.1I, eigenvalues floored at 1e-3. Each test row gets E[x_m | x_o] from its observed numerical cells only, in the frame's scaled space. Categorical columns get the training mode.
- SoftImpute: columns centred on the training means. Rank k is the smallest k whose top eigenvalues of the pairwise covariance reach 90% of its energy, capped at p//2 and p-1. Fit is hard-impute (iterative rank-k SVD) on the training fold: start at 0, at most 100 iterations, tolerance 1e-5. Loadings W = V_k diag(s_k)/sqrt(n). A test row is filled by the PPCA posterior z = (W_o'W_o + s2 I)^-1 W_o'(x_o - mu_o), with s2 the mean of the discarded eigenvalues. Categorical columns get the training mode.
- Added after the seed-42 check on kc2/vehicle and the sklearn cross-check: ice_seq, ice_seq_clip (clipped inside every round to the column's training [min, max], i.e. sklearn's min_value/max_value), condexp_clip and softimpute_clip (clipped at the end). rD.summary:
Verdict flips against the model (K readout), 3-seed means, tie band 0.003:
- kc2_20nan induced is the one clear flip. SoftImpute scores 0.522 against the model's 0.541 and knn5's 0.567, and it sits below the model's K on 3 of 3 seeds, seed-matched against the logged E35 values.
- credit-g_60nan induced is marginal, not a verdict: condexp 0.988 against the model's 0.992 (margin 0.004, 2 of 3 seeds).
- credit-g_80nan adds nothing new: condexp is at about mean_mode (1.000 / 1.004), the model is 1.008, and the model was already above the mean_mode bar.
- With the new arms allowed into the bar, the model is below the bar on 17 of 21 induced variants instead of 19 (the new losses are kc2_20nan, plus the marginal credit-g_60nan). Masked is unchanged at 18 of 21. No new arm beats the model on masked beyond the tie band, except credit-g_80nan, where the model is already above the bar.

Where a new arm would set the bar (below the ADR bar of 5 by more than 0.003):
- Induced, 7 variants:
  - kc2_60nan: SoftImpute 0.600 against 0.717 (3/3 seeds). ice_seq 0.706 also gets under (2/3).
  - kc2_20nan: SoftImpute 0.522 against 0.567 (3/3).
  - vehicle_20nan: condexp 0.451 against 0.473 (3/3).
  - vehicle_60nan: condexp 0.697 (3/3) and SoftImpute 0.685 (2/3) against 0.701.
  - spambase_60nan: condexp 0.975 against 0.984 (3/3).
  - credit-g_60nan: condexp 0.988 against mean_mode's 1.000 (3/3).
  - biodeg_60nan: SoftImpute 0.860 against 0.866. FRAGILE: below on only 1 of 3 seeds.
- Masked, 7 variants:
  - kc2_60nan: SoftImpute 0.582 against 0.717 (3/3).
  - spambase_60nan: condexp 0.956 against 0.982 (2/3).
  - vehicle_20nan: condexp 0.478 and ice_seq 0.484 against 0.505 (3/3).
  - biodeg_60nan: SoftImpute 0.855 against 0.873 (3/3).
  - vehicle_60nan: SoftImpute 0.658 and condexp 0.660 against 0.668 (2/3).
  - credit-g_40nan: condexp 0.990 against 0.997 (2/3).
  - credit-g_60nan: condexp 0.995 against 1.000 (3/3).
- The biggest change in the comparison is on kc2_60nan. The model's margin over the bar shrinks from -0.145 to -0.028 induced and from -0.165 to -0.030 masked. Across the board the arms that do best are low-rank and Gaussian ones on small numerical tables with linear structure: kc2, vehicle, biodeg_60nan and spambase_60nan.

Where the arms are far behind:
- letter, pendigits and electricity score 0.55 to 0.98, against bars of 0.35 to 0.69. These tables are nonlinear, and KNN or hgb wins there.
- credit-g at 20nan and 40nan: ice_seq and condexp are at 0.93 to 1.06, against bars of 0.92 to 1.00.
- At 80nan everything sits at or above mean_mode.
- kr-vs-kp: condexp and SoftImpute are mean_mode by construction, since the table is all categorical. ice_seq (0.67 to 1.04) never beats the lgbm/hgb bar beyond the tie band; it ties at 60nan induced (0.904 against 0.903).
- Against missForest, read apart, the new arms are lower on kc2 (both variants, both populations), on credit-g_60nan and on spambase_60nan masked. They tie it on vehicle_20nan induced.

Overall expectation for a pre-registered study: adding a Gaussian conditional-expectation arm and an inductive low-rank arm would move the bar on roughly a third of the variants. It would cost the model one clear win (kc2_20nan induced) and narrow its margin on kc2_60nan and vehicle. The ADR 0017 picture of the model below the bar on most variants would otherwise stand.

The main methodological result: the template's ICE transform is wrong for linear learners. Its fits are exactly sklearn's, but replaying the kept round's models on test rows that start at the means scores 2 to 19 times mean_mode (spambase_40nan 18.8, kc2_20nan masked 9.9), against 0.65 to 1.1 for sklearn's per-round sequence. Any ICE or MICE arm in the study must specify the sequence transform and a range guard in advance.
caveats: The earlier mice_probe.py numbers inherit the replay defect and are invalid for linear learners. The defect is in the transform at src/training/missforest.py:147-163 (MissForestImputer.impute replays self._models, the kept round's models, under still_converging), not in the fit. On fold 1 of biodeg_20nan and kc2_20nan, replaying sklearn's own last-round models once gives exactly the template's 2.295 / 6.51, while sklearn's sequence transform gives 0.586 / 0.560. The repo's missForest, which uses forests and cannot extrapolate, was not shown to be affected, but its inductive replay is still not what sklearn's transform does. Keep that in mind when reading the ADR 0016/0017 framing of inductive versus transductive.

The ice field is ice_seq, a post-hoc correction of the transform (fit unchanged, not a tuning), added after the seed-42 check. The template's own number is in each note as template_replay. ice_seq uses the template's still_converging round count (3 to 10 per fold), not sklearn's fixed max_iter=10. On vehicle_20nan the two round counts differ by up to 1.19 in individual fills.

Linear arms on heavy-tailed kc2 need a range guard. ice_seq on kc2_20nan masked is 2.96 (seed range 0.64 to 7.40) and condexp is 1.23 to 1.28. Post-hoc clipping to the training range gives 0.541 (ice_seq_clip, inside every round), 0.71 to 0.84 (condexp_clip) and 0.57 (SoftImpute clip). A pre-registered study must fix the clip rule in advance. The clip arms here are diagnostics only and never enter a flag.

The SoftImpute rank rule fails on spambase. The p//2 cap binds at k=28 with only 72 to 86% of the energy, and SoftImpute scores worse than mean_mode at 20nan and 40nan (1.16 / 1.15). That is a failure of the rule, not a verdict on the method. The cap also binds on credit-g (k=3, about 60% energy) and letter (k=8, 85%).

condexp conditions on numerical cells only and fills categorical columns by the mode. Its credit-g numbers (13 of 20 columns categorical) and electricity numbers (1 of 8) therefore understate what a mixed-type Gaussian or MICE arm would reach. On all-categorical kr-vs-kp, condexp and SoftImpute are exactly mean_mode.

ICE's categorical predictors enter as ordinal vocabulary codes (MissForest's _matrix). That misspecifies multi-class columns such as credit-g's purpose for a linear model, and is a plausible reason ICE is worse than mean_mode on credit-g from 40nan up.

condexp uses pairwise-complete covariance with fixed shrinkage and no EM. At 60 to 80% missingness the pairwise estimates rest on few co-observed rows and are noisy, as on biodeg_60nan (condexp 1.069 against SoftImpute 0.860).

These are unpaired, indicative comparisons. The probe numbers come from the backfill's recompute_folds path, as means of per-seed 5-fold means. The model, bar and missForest columns come from ADR 0017's table, which was logged by the live decode path. The seeds (42, 7, 13) and cells are the same, though: knn5 reproduces the logged E35 values within 1e-16 on two variants. So a fold-paired analysis against the E35 children is possible in a real study. The 'n of 3 seeds' counts in the notes compare each seed's arm mean with that seed's logged mean for the ADR-named bar baseline and for the model's K.
The tie band of 0.003 was fixed before any score. A gap just beyond it, such as credit-g_60nan induced at 0.004, should be read as marginal.

merged.headline:
Your literal question (run other algorithms on the same cells and see the gap to TRIDENT) already has an answer for all six baselines the fork has. The ADR 0017 table and probe C's fold-paired rebuild from local artifacts cover all 21 variants. At today's default on seeds 101/202/303 the model is better than the bar of 5 on 14 induced variants, ties on 5 and loses on 2 (credit-g_80nan, electricity_20nan). Against missForest it is 14 better, 6 ties, 1 loss. The loss is credit-g_40nan, and ADR 0019, committed on gorgona8 but 2 commits ahead of your Windows checkout, should remove it. The new information worth having costs little and concerns imputation: probe D shows the linear and low-rank arms (condexp, inductive SoftImpute) set the bar on about a third of the variants. They cost the model its one clear win on kc2_20nan induced, shrink its kc2_60nan margin from -0.145 to -0.028, and drop it from 19/21 to 17/21 induced variants below the bar. ICE/MICE never approaches the model and sits at or above 1.0 at 80nan, so it is a cheap completeness row. Its inherited MissForestImputer.impute replay scores 2 to 19 times mean_mode for linear learners, so it needs a sequential transform. After that comes the first MNAR smoke family: 36 cells on the laptop GPU, MCAR controls included and ledgers kept, which unlocks signed bias, delta-hgb and the t2 split test. Classification is secondary. The fork does have results: a 45-variant default sweep, 0.858/0.799/0.742/0.661/0.531 from 0% to 80% missing, close to Table 4's no-pretraining arm. That makes two wiki pages wrong. Ground rules for every item:
- Pre-register each study with a ticket and an EXPERIMENTATION_LOG entry in the same commit (CLAUDE.md:30-33).
- gorgona8 is the only MLflow writer. Take a SQLite backup before any --apply. Windows runs use --disable_mlflow and a private --metrics_dir.
- The scripts behind probes A to D (barcheck_*, impprobe_*, cls_*, recompute_*) live only in this session's scratchpad. Copy them into a TRIDENT ticket folder before they disappear.

items.expected_outcome:
From probe D:
- kc2_20nan induced: 0.522 against the model's 0.541 and knn5's 0.567, below both on 3/3 seeds. This is the one clear verdict flip against the model.
- kc2_60nan: 0.600 induced and 0.582 masked against a bar of 0.717. The model's margin shrinks from -0.145 to -0.028 (induced) and from -0.165 to -0.030 (masked).
- biodeg_60nan masked: 0.855 vs hgb 0.873 (3/3). Induced: 0.860 vs 0.866, fragile (below on 1/3 seeds).

(1) Canonical SoftImpute is transductive. The inductive projection is a departure to state; fitting on test rows would break the protocol (ADR 0016 Bias).
(2) Rank and shrinkage must come from a rule fixed in advance (ADR 0007 decision 5), not from scored folds.
(3) At 80nan a spambase test row has about 11 of 57 entries observed, so use the posterior or ridge solve, never plain least squares.
(4) The p//2 cap binds on spambase (k=28 at 72-86% energy), credit-g (k=3) and letter (k=8).
(5) The kc2 clip results (0.574) are post-hoc diagnostics unless the clip is pre-registered.
(6) The same boolean-mask and never-edit traps as item 2 apply.

items.name: ICE ('MICE (to add)'): MissForestImputer subclass with linear learners and a sequential per-round transform
items.what:
Three facts settle the design.
(a) Drop the one-hot IterativeImputer. It collapses exactly to mean/mode: n_iter_=1 and 1.000 on every kr-vs-kp fold.
(b) Subclass MissForestImputer and override _fit_one (missforest.py:196-225) with BayesianRidge for numerical targets and multinomial lbfgs LogisticRegression for categorical ones, about 20 lines. Also override impute(): keep every round's models and apply rounds 1..k in order to the test rows, with a per-round clip to the training [min, max]. That is sklearn's transform, D's ice_seq. The inherited impute (missforest.py:147-163) re-applies only the kept round's models, starting from the training means, until still_converging stops. That diverges for linear learners.
(c) With categorical features as ordinal codes this is 'iterativeBR (chained linear conditionals, missForest stopping rule, no posterior draws)'. The categorical-correct version, from wf2's MICE card, uses one-hot features with the target's own block excluded plus multinomial LR. Pre-register which one is the thesis row; the categorical-correct one belongs in the promotion item.
Use sklearn IterativeImputer(BayesianRidge) with a matched round count as the test oracle on the numeric-only tables.

items.expected_outcome:
A cheap completeness row, not a threat to the model's lead. Its 3-seed mean is never below the model's K on any variant; on the variants D flagged it is below on 0 of 3 seeds.

At 80nan it is at or above 1.0 on every table: credit-g 1.134/1.118, kr-vs-kp 1.010/1.041, spambase 1.052/1.354 (induced/masked).

It reaches the bar in only two places: vehicle_20nan masked (0.484 vs knn5 0.505, 3/3 seeds) and kc2_60nan induced (0.706 vs 0.717, 2/3). It ties hgb on kr-vs-kp_60nan induced (0.904 vs 0.903).

On credit-g it scores at or above 0.93, and above 1.0 from 40nan, because ordinal codes feed a linear model.

kc2_20nan masked scores 2.96 unclipped and 0.541 with the per-round clip. The template replay scores 2.0-18.8 on the numerical tables (spambase_40nan 18.8). This agrees with CACTI's MICE at about 1.12x Mean.
items.traps:
(1) The replay defect: using the inherited impute() gives invalid numbers. The earlier mice_probe.py and the critic's 20-line probe (credit-g_60nan 1.466) both inherit it.
(2) Round count: D used still_converging (3-10 rounds per fold). Default sklearn max_iter=10 differs by up to 1.19 in single fills on vehicle_20nan, so pre-register the count.
(3) BayesianRidge and lbfgs are deterministic, so the global streams stay untouched (ADR 0007 decision 6). Check it anyway with the test_missforest.py pattern.
(4) A committed version needs hand-written sklearn.linear_model stubs under strict mypy; stubs/sklearn has no linear_model.
(5) Name it 'ice' or 'iterativeBR', not MICE: impute_score rewards conditional means, and posterior draws add noise.
(6) Side question: missForest uses the same replay. Forests can't extrapolate, so D showed no harm, and ADR 0016 bounds the inductive-vs-transductive difference at 0.016. An optional 'missforest_seq' arm on the small tables in item 5 checks this. It is memory-heavy on spambase because every round's forests are kept.

items.what:
Subclass GradientBoostingImputer the way LightGbmImputer does. Override impute: call super().impute(frame, hidden), then add delta_j * sd_j to numerical fills only where frame.isna() (real gaps), never on hidden & ~isna (eval-mask cells, which are MCAR). Two variants:
- an oracle delta computed on the training fold from the _00nan sibling, labelled as oracle;
- a fixed grid of 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 sd.
Score offline through recompute_folds on item 7's variants. recompute_folds resolves the _00nan sibling for the new names.

items.name: MaCoDE (owner-decided deep baseline), vendored with an inductive wrapper
items.what:
Vendor macode/model.py and the parts of dataset.py and macode.py you need, about 400 lines, MIT notice kept, under src/training/.
- Guard the empty-group torch.stack.
- Switch to AdamW with weight decay 1e-3.
- Drop the global reseeding (use fork_rng with the cudnn flags saved and restored).
- Copy the frame instead of mutating it.
Then write MacodeImputer.fit/impute:
- fit builds an hgb-style training vocabulary and fits the bins on the training fold;
- impute encodes the test frame through the stored scalers and bins, sets hidden|isna to index 0, runs batched no_grad passes, and decodes by posterior mean (sum of p_l * bin mean) for numerics and argmax for categoricals; a sampled-draw arm can be logged separately.
Use the paper's settings: bins 50, d 128, 4 heads, 2 layers, 500 epochs, batch 1024. Score through recompute_folds(fold_scorer=...).

items.name: GBDT-MIA bar (LightGBM and HGB with native NaN; XGBoost if the lock pin is approved) on the sweep's exact folds
items.what:
A scratch script over the 45 variants:
1. prepare_dataset(DatasetSpec.from_name(v, None)), then build_folds(frame, 'class', 3, 42). These rebuild the sweep's folds exactly; verified on 16 fold children across 8 variants.
2. Per fold, fit LGBMClassifier and HistGradientBoostingClassifier, both with class_weight='balanced' and early stopping on fold.validation_indices. LightGBM 4.7 uses eval_set plus callbacks=[early_stopping]; sklearn 1.9's HGB.fit accepts X_val/y_val.
3. Build the input matrix from the training-fold vocabulary inside the script, with NaN for missing or unseen values.
4. Score test with build_fold_result and pair per fold with the sweep's f1_macro.
5. Optionally add a 30-minute single-split run (cv_folds=None) against Table 3's LightGBM and XGBoost columns.

conflicts_resolved.topic: How long the classification harness takes
conflicts_resolved.positions: wf2 gbdt card: 2-3 h. wf2 deep-tabular card: 6-10 h. wf2 report-reuse card: 8-16 h for reporting alone.
conflicts_resolved.resolution:
These are three different deliverables, not one disagreement.
- 2-3 h: a scratch GBDT loop over build_folds that writes a CSV, plus 1-2 h for a reader pairing it with the existing 3-fold sweep (item 14). This exists today because the TRIDENT side was already trained.
- 6-10 h: a committed, strict-mypy harness with per-fold encoding for neural baselines (FT-Transformer, TabNet). Not needed for GBDT.
- 8-16 h: server-side logging plus a paired 15-fold report. Only needed once 5-fold, 3-seed TRIDENT classification cells exist.
The report card's premise that 'there is no classification result in the fork' is false.

conflicts_resolved.positions: wf2: the classifier is QUICK, because the v2 weights are ungated (Prior-Labs/TabPFN-v2-clf/-reg, Apache 2.0 plus attribution). wf1 and ADR 0016: NOT_QUICK because of licence acceptance and TABPFN_TOKEN on headless gorgona8, plus the 10k-row limit.
conflicts_resolved.resolution:
Both hold for different versions. The token and non-commercial blocker applies only to 2.5 and later; v2 is ungated if ModelVersion.V2 and the package version are pinned, so ADR 0016's token half is stale for v2. Its 10k-row and 10-class half stands: letter and electricity are outside v2's envelope.
- Classifier: quick in code (6-10 h), but only half a comparison, and classification is secondary now. Not in the list.
- Extension imputer (TabPFNUnsupervisedModel): about 1,000 GPU-h and sampled output. Not quick.
- Column-wise subclass: 5-8 h plus 6-10 GPU-h. Tier C, item 12.
It still needs a separate venv or an owner-approved lock change.

conflicts_resolved.positions: wf2 hyperimpute card: MEDIUM, via a --no-deps install with a trimmed GAIN/MIWAE/SoftImpute/Sinkhorn path of about 5 h. wf1, plus wf2's own mice card and ADR 0016: NOT_QUICK.

conflicts_resolved.topic: MICE: IterativeImputer (QUICK) vs a hand-rolled round loop (MEDIUM) vs a ~20-line MissForestImputer subclass
conflicts_resolved.positions: wf1 rank 1: one-hot IterativeImputer, 60-80 lines. Verdict: one-hot collapses to mean/mode; build a round-loop clone (half a day; missforest.py-sized). wf2: hand-rolled ICE with one-hot features excluding the target's own block, 1-2 days with family and backfill. Critic: a ~20-line _fit_one subclass, with probe values (credit-g_60nan 1.466).
conflicts_resolved.resolution:
Probe D settles it.
- One-hot IterativeImputer is refuted (n_iter_=1, exactly 1.000 on kr-vs-kp).
- The 20-line subclass is right about _fit_one, but the inherited MissForestImputer.impute (missforest.py:147-163, checked) re-applies only the kept round's models from the mean start. For linear learners that scores 2-19x mean_mode, so the critic's credit-g number is the defect.
- Correct probe: the subclass plus an overridden sequential per-round impute plus a range clip, about half a day (item 4), checked against IterativeImputer to 1.4e-9.
- The categorical-correct design (wf2's one-hot features with own-block exclusion and multinomial LR) belongs with promotion (item 6, 1.5-2 days). IterativeImputer stays only as the numeric test oracle.

conflicts_resolved.topic: Can imputation baselines be computed on Windows?
conflicts_resolved.positions: OPS-7: no. The cache keys on the hostname, KNN/hgb digits drift by machine, and writing the pulled store breaks the hand-off. Probes C and D: computed on Windows anyway (D reproduced knn5 within 1.1e-16 and mean_mode within 4e-16, and left the repo byte-identical).
conflicts_resolved.resolution:
Both, for different purposes.
- Windows is fine for indicative and design numbers: offline recompute_folds(fold_scorer=...) with no cache dir and no store, and for wrapper development and --disable_mlflow smokes.
- Any number that will be logged into MLflow or frozen in the thesis comes from gorgona8: through item 5's pass (cache hits for lgbm and missForest), through a backfill --apply, or through a fresh default sweep.
- On Windows the lgbm/missForest cache always misses, which costs 5-10 CPU-h.
- The deterministic numpy arms will likely agree across machines up to BLAS last digits. Check before relying on it.

not_quick.name: ReMasker (clean-room fork-native)
not_quick.why: No LICENSE file, so it can only be reimplemented clean-room (17-24 h). The stock code parses sys.argv, calls sys.exit(1) on a non-finite loss, and never seeds. Training hits a 0/0 loss, near-certain on credit-g_80nan, kr-vs-kp_60/80nan, spambase_60/80nan, vehicle_60nan and biodeg_60nan. It is numeric-only. 15-25 GPU-h at 300 epochs for 63 (variant, seed) pairs off-store, or about 40 GPU-h per BACKLOG I3. Do it after MaCoDE; the BACKLOG I3 design is ready.

not_quick.name: HyperImpute package (AutoML imputer, GAIN, MIWAE, Sinkhorn)
TabImpute zero-shot
not_quick.why: Pins tabpfn==6.0.0, which needs sklearn<1.8 against the fork's 1.9: a separate venv plus a subprocess bridge. No code licence. Transductive in context, and the paper's setting reads the global RNG. Only 6 of 21 variants (kc2, vehicle, biodeg) are in its validated regime. Categorical support is unvalidated and its categorical scripts are broken. 12-20 h. No published MNAR specialist weights.

not_quick.name: TabPFN extension imputer (tabpfn-extensions TabPFNUnsupervisedModel.impute)
not_quick.why: Cost is quadratic in the number of columns: about 7.6M TabPFN calls, roughly 1,000 GPU-h, or about 100 in fast mode. The output is a stochastic sample. It pulls in telemetry and has no device handling. Use the column-wise subclass (item 12) instead.

not_quick.name: not-MIWAE, GINA, NIMIWAE, Heckman imputer
not_quick.why:
All are blocked on item 7's MNAR family: on today's MCAR holes a selection model is only a misspecification control.
- not-MIWAE: the MIT PyTorch port lacks multi-class categorical heads and needs a real-vs-artificial mask split. 18-28 h, 20-50 device-h.
- GINA: archived 2020-era code. It needs fully observed auxiliary columns, which the fork's all-column injector never leaves.
- NIMIWAE: GPL-3, R/reticulate, hard-coded CUDA.
- Heckman: 12-20 h, fragile identification under self-masking.
Delta-adjusted hgb (item 10) gives most of the cheap insight.

not_quick.name: CACTI/CMAE and DiffPuter
not_quick.why:
CACTI: GPL-3, CLI-only, a separate conda environment and a language-model download. Under MCAR its copy masking reduces to ReMasker's random masking. Its idea (CMAE) costs 3-5 h inside a ReMasker reimplementation once MNAR exists.
DiffPuter: a dataset-specific script, about 1,000-2,500 s per fit (100-200 GPU-h for the grid), with NaN and non-convergence failures on small tables. At most a later 15-30 GPU-h slice on the three large 20nan tables.

not_quick.name: Distributional metrics (sliced Wasserstein, energy distance) on today's MCAR default
not_quick.why: They need all 5 fold ledgers. MLflow keeps only the best and worst folds (a biased subset). The rest sit in the server queues' $STATE/results directories, which no sync pulls and which may have been cleaned. Current-default ledgers cover 7 of 21 variants, and baseline fills are never persisted. Feasible path: compute them on item 7's laptop cells, whose ledgers are all local, or after the deterministic rerun below.

not_quick.name: Deterministic rerun of the 63 default cells with --save_model and train/validation ledgers
not_quick.why: A TRIDENT retrain (about 7-8 h on gorgona8) plus a hook in decoding.py. It unlocks true impute-then-learn (Le Morvan & Varoquaux), full-coverage ledgers and the cosine probe. Worth doing; it pairs naturally with item 5's fresh-sweep alternative. Medium, not quick.

not_quick.name: TRIDENT classification at 5 folds x 3 seeds, and the validation-ranked retune (step zero proper)
not_quick.why: The 5-fold, 3-seed run is cheap in code (1-2 h; clone gap_token_run.py without decode_gap_token, as config.py:276-281 rejects it for classification) but costs a server night. The validation retune needs a change to opt.py: classification ranks trials on test macro-F1 (types.py:138, opt.py:175-179), and finetuning.py never returns validation F1. It also needs an ADR and tens of GPU-hours. Secondary to imputation; run it on otherwise idle server nights only.

not_quick.name: t2 tied-token arms and the Table 4 imputation-variant arm for classification
not_quick.why: Both touch the protected classification path. Fine-tuning always shows [NULL] (finetuning.py:81-88, 122-124). A default-off flag plus plumbing is about 60 lines (commit d0744ad precedent), half a day to a day, and it needs a classification reference first.

not_quick.name: Equal-budget HPO (TabZilla-style, 20 trials) and deep classification baselines (FT-Transformer, TabNet, native SAINT, NAIM)
not_quick.why: The GBDT half of the HPO is quick (2-3 h), but the TRIDENT half needs the opt.py change. The deep baselines need the 6-10 h harness plus 3-16 h each. All are classification and secondary under the imputation focus.

not_quick.name: miceforest
not_quick.why: With mean matching off it is essentially ADR 0016's withdrawn missforest_lgbm; with it on, it is stochastic. It is a new dependency. Keep it in reserve as a multiple-imputation generator for the classification side.

Week 2, laptop: vendor MaCoDE (item 11, 10-14 h) and smoke it on CPU with credit-g and vehicle. Then run the 315-fit grid off-store on gorgona8 (3-5 GPU-h) in a slot the GPU queue leaves free.
Week 2, owner decision: approve or decline a separate venv for tabpfn pinned to ModelVersion.V2. If approved, build item 12 (5-8 h) and run it on gorgona8 (6-10 GPU-h).

Classification in gaps only: on the laptop CPU whenever it is idle, items 14 and 15 (the GBDT-MIA bar plus impute+indicator on the sweep's folds, about 4-6 h code, a few CPU-hours).
